newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end firmer, resources favoured.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end firmer, resources favoured.

text.p: Australian shares finished higher on Thursday with gains underpinned by a stronger resource sector which was buoyed by firmer metal prices and takeover activity in the gold sector.
The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 9.6 points firmer at 2,386.3.
Turnover was lifted by a heavy activity in the gold sector following bids for Papua New Guinea gold miner Highlands Gold and Placer Pacific by Canada's Placer Dome Inc.

"There was a buying frenzy in gold stocks spurred by the takeover offers and the excitement surrounding discoveries in the Gawler Craton - This was definitely the driving force behind the market's gains today," said Joseph Pagliaro, client advisor at Brisbane brokerage, Wilson HTM.
Pagliaro said the substantial interest in the gold sector rubbed off on other resource sectors as investor optimism rose.
"I think it will settle down tommorrow but the price of gold is due for a bounce," he said.
Dealers said trade was likely to be quiet on Friday due to the closure of U.S. markets for the Thanksgiving day holiday.

Canadian gold group, Placer Dome Inc's bid for Papua New Guinea (PNG) gold miners Highlands Gold and the remaining 25 percent of Placer Pacific caused a rush on the stock of other PNG gold stocks with Goldfields and Lihir Gold bid much higher.
Lihir stock closed nine cents higher at A$2.40 (US$1.94) and Goldfields shares ended 14 cents up at A$2.60.
The gold sector was the outstanding market segment on the day while big resource stocks BHP and CRA underpinned the market's gains after the price of copper continued to recover.

Brisbane-based pastoral company Primac was one of the most active stocks with fellow pastoral group Elders buying a strategic 17 percent stake following a hostile takeover offer for Primac from Perth-based IAMA in September.
Primac shares finished 15 cents firmer at A$3.20.
